customManagers.description: Track the vendored tunnel binaries' upstream versions in app/tunnel-binaries.lock. Renovate proposes a version bump when upstream cuts a release; the binary is then rebuilt+re-hosted and re-pinned by the 'Release tunnel binaries' workflow (which reads its versions from this same lock).

packageRules.description: Group non-major Gradle/AGP/Kotlin/library updates (from gradle/libs.versions.toml and app/build.gradle.kts) into a single PR. Major bumps (e.g. AGP or Kotlin major versions) are left ungrouped since they often need manual migration.

Group GitHub Actions SHA/digest and version bumps into a single PR. helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests (above) keeps `uses:` pinned to full commit SHAs with the version comment, which is what keeps .github/workflows zizmor-clean.

Vendored tunnel binaries (app/tunnel-binaries.lock): a version bump here is a PROPOSAL — it is not shippable until the binary is rebuilt at that version, re-hosted, and its digests refreshed. Run the 'Release tunnel binaries' workflow (it reads versions from the lock and prints the new tag/base_url/digests to paste back), then run scripts/gen-third-party-notices.py. Never automerge: these open network tunnels on the car. One PR per binary so each can be rebuilt independently.
zrok must stay on v1.x — v2 renamed the command to cmd/zrok2 and is a breaking change for ZrokLauncher.

MANUAL ONLY — do not touch. openh264Version/openh264Sha256 and opencvMobileVersion/opencvMobileSha256/opencvMobileTag in app/build.gradle.kts are not normal package-manager dependencies: they are digest-pinned native binaries fetched by the bespoke downloadOpenH264/downloadOpenCV Gradle tasks and checked against the hardcoded SHA-256 in verifyDigest(). Bumping the version string without also re-deriving and updating the matching SHA-256 (and re-auditing the artifact) would either break the build's digest check or silently accept an unverified binary. These are intentionally excluded from every manager and must be updated by hand.
